articles.title: Mahadev betting app promoter Sourabh Chandrakar extradited from Oman, to face Raipur CBI court today
articles.summary: Mahadev betting app promoter Sourabh Chandrakar extradited from Oman after Interpol notice; to appear in Raipur CBI court in illegal betting case.
articles.body: RAIPUR: Mahadev betting app promoter Sourabh Chandrakar, accused of running an illegal online betting network from abroad and paying protection money to public servants, has been extradited from Oman, the CBI said on Sunday. A special CBI team escorted him to India, and he is scheduled to be produced before a special court in Raipur on Monday.Chandrakar is wanted in two CBI cases in which chargesheets have been filed, as well as an Enforcement Directorate (ED) case in which a prosecution complaint has been submitted. He will undergo a medical examination before being taken to Raipur after transit remand is obtained, the agency said.The Royal Oman Police located and detained Chandrakar on the basis of an Interpol Red Corner Notice, according to CBI. The CBI and ED subsequently submitted formal extradition requests supported by evidence gathered against him. After Oman approved the extradition, a CBI team travelled to Muscat to bring him back.The CBI took over the Mahadev Online Book cases at the Chhattisgarh govt’s request and has described the operation as one of the country’s largest illegal online betting syndicates. Investigators allege that it was run from outside India through franchised “panels” and “branches” that enrolled users and collected bets on cricket, football, card games and other events.The agency alleged that betting proceeds were routed through numerous mule bank accounts, layered through multiple transactions and transferred abroad through hawala channels. Part of the money was allegedly paid to public servants to allow the network to operate without interference.Chandrakar is among the key accused named in chargesheets filed under the Prevention of Corruption Act, IPC provisions relating to criminal conspiracy, cheating and forgery, and the Chhattisgarh Gambling (Prohibition) Act. articles.title: NWSL Decision Day: Gotham secures Shield with win over Utah Royals, Seattle Reign squeak into last playoff spot
articles.summary: The final seeding for the playoffs came down the final minutes of the 2026 NWSL season.
articles.body:
The 2026 NWSL regular season went out with a bang, with several results shaking up the table on a busy Decision Day. Gotham FC won its first Shield with a 2-0 win over the Utah Royals, while a 1-0 victory over the Orlando Pride was enough to help the Seattle Reign clinch a playoff spot.

Both the NWSL Shield and the final playoff slot came down to the final day of play, with Gotham hoping to edge out the second-place San Diego Wave and the Reign hoping to lock up a return to the postseason. The league entered Sunday with seven of the eight playoff spots already filled, but with plenty of ways that things could shake out.

It didn't take long for Gotham to pull ahead against the Utah Royals, as Guro Reiten found the back of the net in the ninth minute of play. Jaedyn Shaw then sealed their chances with another goal in the 80th minute.

Gotham, which has won two of the past three NWSL Championships, will now add its first NWSL Shield to the trophy case. The team finishes with 61 points and a 18W-7D-5L record.

Down in the middle of the table, the eighth and final postseason slot came down to three teams: the Reign, the North Carolina Courage and the Denver Summit. With the Courage and the Summit playing against each other to end the year, Seattle needed to win-and-in on Decision Day to keep its season going.

Despite dominating the game, the Reign couldn't find the back of the net until the 68th minute, when Seattle defender Jordyn Bugg hit a beautiful strike that barreled past Pride keeper Cosette Morché. The Reign immediately celebrated, knowing that it could likely be enough to clinch.

Extending the season took on extra weight in Seattle, as Sunday was the final home match for club legend Jess Fishlock, who will be retiring after this year . (Seattle, as the eighth-seeded postseason team, will not host a playoff game.)

Moments after the Reign officially won, North Carolina finally broke the stalemate with Denver thanks to an own goal from Kaleigh Kurtz — but it was too late for the Courage, who fell just one spot short of the playoffs. North Carolina forward and 2026 Golden Boot winner Ashley Sanchez, who tied the NWSL single-season record for goals with 20, was forced to see her MVP-caliber season come to an unexpectedly early end.

Meanwhile, the rest of the eight-game slate had significant implications. The Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current picked up key wins to secure home-field advantage for the quarterfinals. Angel City FC jumped the crowded middle of the table with a dominant 4-1 win over the Boston Legacy.

San Diego Wave FC — 58 points, 18W-4D-8L

Washington Spirit — 55 points, 17W-4D-9L

Kansas City Current — 53 points, 16W-5D-9L

Portland Thorns FC — 50 points, 14W-8D-8L

Seattle Reign FC — 47 points, 14W-5D-11L

articles.title: East Bengal women off to winning start at AFC Women's Champions League
articles.summary: Kolkata: East Bengal women's team began their Mission Asia on a perfect note, defeating Vietnamese champions Ho Chi Minh City WFC 2-1 in their Group B
articles.body: Kolkata: East Bengal women's team began their Mission Asia on a perfect note, defeating Vietnamese champions Ho Chi Minh City WFC 2-1 in their Group B opener of the AFC Women's Champions League here on Sunday.Ugandan striker Fazila Ikwaput was the chief architect of the hosts' win at Kishore Bharati Krirangan, scoring both goals in the first half and setting the Moshal Girls on track for a historic last-8 spot in the continent's premier women's club football. There were some nervy moments, especially when Ho Chi Minh City reduced the margin through Dau Nguyen Quynh Anh on the hour mark. However, there was a statement of intent in their performance and coach Anthony Andrews' no-nonsense approach to the game by starting with six foreigners paid off handsomely in the end.The Indian football also got its first taste of a VAR-like system in the day's first match in which North Korean champions 4.25 Sports Club got the better of their South Korean rivals Hwacheon KSPO WFC 2-1. - Nilesh.Bhattacharya@timesofindia.comGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: China state broadcaster CCTV pulls Real Madrid match over Mbappé joke
articles.summary: China Media Group, which acknowledged Mbappé's apology, has not said how long the blackout will last.
articles.body:
China's state broadcaster CCTV did not air a Real Madrid match on Sunday, despite the club's star striker Kylian Mbappé's apology for his "ill-judged" remarks on the late Chinese leader Mao Zedong.

Mbappé drew huge backlash after saying the meme "that makes [him] laugh the most" was the one in which his face is superimposed on a "Chinese dictator" resembling Mao.

China Media Group, CCTV's parent organisation, said last Tuesday it would suspend broadcasts of Spanish football La Liga matches following the furore, which also led to Mbappé being dropped by several Chinese brands.

China's foreign ministry had said it took Mbappé's apology "seriously". Real Madrid and La Liga have also apologised.

China Media Group had earlier demanded apologies from the three parties, calling them "an absolute prerequisite" for moving past the incident.

It has acknowledged the apologies, but has not commented on how long the broadcast blackout will last.

Mbappé, who reportedly made his remark about the meme on French talk show The Bridge, apologised later on Tuesday.

"My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world," he had said.

The joke did not go down well in China, where Mao is revered by the Communist Party, despite his having overseen one of the bloodiest chapters in the country's past.

Mao, who led the Chinese Communist Party to victory in the civil war and founded the People's Republic of China, died in 1976.

During his rule he oversaw the Great Leap Forward and the Cultural Revolution, which led to a famine that killed tens of millions and unleashed violent purges across Chinese society.

This is not the first time Beijing has suspended sports broadcasts over political sensitivities.

It pulled NBA games for a year from October 2019 after Daryl Morey, the general manager of Houston Rockets, tweeted in support of Hong Kong protesters during widespread pro-democracy protests in the city.

Morey backtracked on his comment after fierce criticism from Chinese fans, sponsors and commercial partners.

"I have had a lot of opportunity since that tweet to hear and consider other perspectives," Morey later wrote.

"I have always appreciated the significant support our Chinese fans and sponsors...I would hope that those who are upset will know that offending or misunderstanding them was not my intention."

Real Madrid beat Racing Santander 3-0 in Sunday's match, with goals from Mbappé, Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomande.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo rested for Al-Nassr's Uzbekistan trip amid growing security concerns
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo will miss Al-Nassr's AFC Champions League match against Pakhtakor in Uzbekistan as the Saudi Arabian club looks to manage its players'
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo will miss Al-Nassr's AFC Champions League match against Pakhtakor in Uzbekistan as the Saudi Arabian club looks to manage its players' workload amid a busy schedule and travel demands. The Portuguese superstar has been left out of the squad by coach Ange Postecoglou for Monday's match in Tashkent. Kingsley Coman and Mohamed Simakan have also been rested.Ronaldo was in fine form last week, scoring a hat-trick in a Saudi Pro League match to take his career goal tally to 985. However, he will not be part of Al-Nassr's squad for the continental fixture.Postecoglou, who previously coached Tottenham Hotspur and Australia, explained the decision at a news conference in Uzbekistan.He said Ronaldo, Coman and Simakan had been rested “given the pressure of matches and the amount of travel involved.”Al-Nassr looking to improve Champions League positionAl-Nassr are chasing their first-ever Asian title but have struggled in the competition so far. They are currently ninth in the western zone standings, making them the lowest-ranked among the five Saudi Arabian clubs taking part in the 32-team tournament.The competition is divided into two groups of 16 teams, with the eastern and western zones having separate standings. The top eight teams from each zone will qualify for the knockout stage.Despite the slow start, Postecoglou believes his team are making progress.“Despite the difficult start, the preparation conditions, and the lack of complete readiness at the beginning of the season, we have now reached an excellent stage,” Postecoglou added.Security concerns affect Asian competitionsRonaldo also missed Al-Nassr's previous Champions League fixture last week after UAE club Al-Wasl refused to travel to Riyadh for the match. The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) subsequently postponed the game.Security concerns have also affected Al-Nassr's home fixtures. Their previous home match in the competition on October 12 was delayed by an hour following reports of missile attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels.The situation has raised concerns about the future of other Asian football competitions, including the Asian Cup scheduled to begin in Saudi Arabia on January 7.The Houthis have launched several attacks on Saudi Arabia, adding to concerns about the security situation in the region.Japan raise doubts over Asian CupJapan Football Association president Tsuneyasu Miyamoto has expressed doubts about whether the Asian Cup can go ahead in Saudi Arabia as planned.“Based on what I’ve learned from the news, the situation is still unsafe, so at this point, I don’t think it would be easy to hold the (Asian) Cup there,” Miyamoto said at an AFC Congress last month.His comments came after AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa said the organisation would continue to monitor the situation before making a final decision.“We can wait until the end of November,” Salman said. “Things can change very quickly for better or worse in the region, and it is a question of seeing what happens.“If we need to make a decision then we will, but we could move back a year to 2028 if we need to.”Saudi organisers, however, have maintained that preparations are continuing as planned. The kick-off times and venues for all matches were finalised last week.Other Saudi clubs in Champions League actionMeanwhile, Al-Ahli, who have won the last two Asian titles, are third in their group ahead of their away match against Qatar's Al-Sadd.The Jeddah-based club suffered a heavy 6-1 defeat at home on Friday but are expected to have England striker Ivan Toney available for the next match.Toney, who has scored 13 league goals this season, travelled to London last week to attend court, where he pleaded not guilty to an assault charge.Elsewhere, Al-Hilal continued their winning run in the Saudi Pro League. England forward Ollie Watkins scored as the Riyadh-based club registered their fifth consecutive league victory to move to the top of the standings.The four-time Asian champions will host UAE side Shabab Al-Ahli in their next continental fixture. While that match is expected to go ahead, concerns remain over the security situation and its possible impact on the Asian Cup.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Fantasy Football: Key offseason narratives take shape on Sunday in Week 8
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Chris Allen examines some storylines coming off Week 8's Sunday action.
articles.body:
Every Sunday, I'm somehow surprised and not surprised at the same time. The action keeps me on the edge of my seat. A tipped pass here, a missed tackle (or many) there and my mood swings with every snap. In the moment, it all feels random.

But once the dust settles, I can usually trace the path. The signs were there. A target share creeping up in September. A run game that never looked right in camp. An offensive line we all worried about in August. We just didn't know when those threads would finally come together or fall apart.

That's where we are after Week 8. Some of the biggest storylines from Sunday felt like shocks while they were happening. But if we look back at a few of the narratives we were debating in the offseason and September, they shouldn't have caught us off guard. So, let's check in on those early takes and see which ones are paying off.

Here's a quick peek behind the curtain. During the first window of Sunday games, I'm taking notes and going back and forth with the crew on what will go into this piece and the theme. I couldn't concentrate after about 4 p.m. ET.

Almost any other week, Joe Burrow leading a game-winning drive in OT would only lower my life expectancy by a year or two. Finally, there's a positive data point in the "is Burrow clutch" argument. Throwing for 462 yards and zipping five TD passes to his pass-catchers isn't bad either. But Burrow threw some of the gas on the fire with multiple turnovers , causing me to yell incoherently at my office wall.

However, the largest problem was on the other side of the ball.

Pressure Rate: 37.0% (Weeks 1-7), 19.0% (against TEN)

Rushing Yards per Game Surrendered: 80.5, 117.0

Passing Success Rate Allowed: 52.0%, 66.0%

To be fair, a couple of the offseason defensive additions showed up when the situation looked bleak. DT Dexter Lawrence sacked Cam Ward, taking the Titans out of FG range and he almost had a scoop-and-score at the start of the second half. DE Boye Mafe set up the turnover. But Tennessee hadn't scored more than 35 points in a game since Week 17 of '21. Ward's highest single-game passing yardage total was 265 until he came to Paycor Stadium. The idea that the Bengals could turn around their defense in a single year now seems, in Step Brothers terms , a little messed up. And Cincinnati's response on offense looked all too familiar.

As I mentioned on Friday, unless DC Al Golden can bring his unit back to even close to league average, just give me more pass-catchers for Burrow . Seven of Chase Brown's 12 carries went for three or fewer yards. Samaje Perine averaged 2.5 YPC while playing 58.8% of the red-zone snaps. All while playing against a defense that came into Week 8 allowing 104.9 YPG to opposing RBs.

Meanwhile, the Bengals used three-WR sets at a season-high 64.3% rate, and got their young pass-catchers into the mix. Rookie TE Jack Endries got his first TD, and WR Dohnte Meyers ran a route on 66.0% of Burrow's dropbacks, picking up a key first down to keep them alive.

Instead of mortgaging its future to fix its ground game, Cincinnati should invest in what makes them a problem for opposing defenses and make Burrow the MVP candidate he's looked like for years.

The Raiders are in a constant "it's so over — we're so back" loop. They brought Klint Kubiak after he orchestrated Seattle's Super Bowl run. But Brock Bowers, their best offensive weapon, needed a meniscus trim before playing a regular-season snap. Kirk Cousins goes on a three-game winning streak, then a trio of losses put us on "Mendoza Watch." Sure, facing the Jets is a get-right spot for most teams. But I don't remember Cousins showing this same type of swagger last year.

Maybe swagger is the wrong descriptor. I'm not completely sure because I don't know what Cousins is doing after his second TD pass. If there's a name for his celly, somebody let me know. Anyway, Cousins operating Kubiak's scheme to near perfection isn't a revelation, after the two worked together in Minnesota. Cousins hit a season-high play-action rate (40.6%), and it was the third straight outing with the personnel grouping requiring at least two TEs on the field. He averaged 1.06 EPA per attempt to the MoF. And seeing the guy responsible for most of the production also isn't much of a shock.

Betting on Kubiak was a bet on him making his top pass-catcher an unguardable weapon. He's lived up to the expectation so far. Bowers just getting to 70 yards for the sixth consecutive game was an accolade on its own. But his utility to the offense goes past how far Bowers moves the ball.

Since coming back to the lineup in Week 3, Bowers ranks 11th amongst all pass-catchers in first downs per route run (12.6%). He sits right between Amon-Ra St. Brown and Ja'Marr Chase in that metric. The "TE-WR" is also just inside the top 12 in YPRR ahead of Chase and CeeDee Lamb. And this is all while running just eight fewer routes from the outside than Tee Higgins. A change in coaching is working out for the passing game as we envisioned.

That last sentence had most folks scratching their head well into the second quarter. Jeanty's output as a rusher has been a cause for concern since Week 1. After cracking the century mark against the Dolphins, Jeanty hasn't crossed 60 yards in a game since, and his yards on the ground have receded each week. He's continued to redeem himself as a receiver , but Mike Washington Jr. continues to steal snaps and carries. Washington's moved the chains more often and has a higher success rate on early downs than Jeanty. With his weekly workload rising, Washington will have FLEX appeal in this expanded version of the Raiders' backfield.

It's Not Just Wilson and Hall in New York Anymore

We weren't targeting any of the Jets' skill players until the third or fourth round for a couple of reasons. First, we assumed the team would lag behind the division, but bringing back Geno Smith would stabilize the situation. Second, and more importantly, the idea was that the targets and touches would consolidate on Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall. I get that Hall's quad injury has kept him off the field. But even if Hall were active, he might be in the same situation as Jeanty.

Braelon Allen has averaged 22 touches per game with Hall out. He's churned out more than 100 scrimmage yards in four of five starts. That's while opposing defenses have put eight or more in the box on 46.2% of his carries (fifth-highest rate among active starters). It's also after defenders have met Allen at or behind the LOS on 48 of his totes (only Bucky Irving and Derrick Henry have more). And still, you'll find Allen's name in the rank where we'd expect to see Hall's.

Rushing Success Rate: 48.4%, 3rd (out of 19 qualifiers – min. 50% team rushing rate)

Adj. Yards After Contact per Att.: 4.6, 2nd

Smith's return has done more for their aerial attack than anticipated, too. Luckily, a sideline exchange and spending time with his QB after the game got Wilson's target rate back up over 20%. But during each contest, a few extra names have come into the picture.

Obvious Passing Situations: 14.8% (Mitchell), 11.5% (Taylor), 9.8% (Sadiq)

Downfield: 27.6% (Mitchell), 13.8% (Williams), 10.6% (Cooper)

Red Zone: 16.7% (Williams), 16.7% (Taylor), 16.7% (Sadiq)

Adonai Mitchell is the latest contestant on the "Who's the Jets' WR2" game show. After Omar Cooper Jr. took the title in Week 7, the former Colt turned nine targets into 142 yards. But Mitchell's 25-yard aDOT should have anyone reconsidering slotting him into their WR3 spot in Week 9. While Smith has been willing to let the ball fly downfield, a positive result isn't always in the cards. Plus, with the Jets facing the Chiefs, Wilson should lead the Jets in targets yet again.

It Was All About The Young Boys at RB for Broncos and Chiefs

The battle for the AFC West totaled 543 passing yards and five TDs. Patrick Mahomes was the first QB to complete three TD passes against Denver. Bo Nix was ripping passes to Jaylen Waddle downfield. The game came down to the final play.

But the two players that stood out were the rookies, not the vets.

Well, I did say last Friday that Mahomes needed another receiver . And granted, the Broncos defense isn't the best place to find out if you're on the same page as your QB. But both Andrew Armstrong and Jalen Royals ran fewer routes on Sunday than when they played the Seahawks. Cyrus Allen got in some more cardio, but earned just one more target. In short, the environment was conducive to more RB targets, but instead of Kenneth Walker III doing most of the damage, Emmett Johnson became The Engine of the offense.

I know a single game can skew rate stats. But there was more to Johnson's 187-yard outburst than taking a screen pass to the house. The first-year rusher broke six tackles across his six touches on the day. His lone carry went for 15 yards. While we can't expect half of his touches to turn into explosive gains every week, establishing himself as the ideal backup to Walker (with a rushing and receiving skill set) should put him on everyone's radar as a bench stash.

But for Denver, if you got its RB1 off waivers, you've found an every-week starter.

If I've preached anything, it's about applying context before reacting. Jonah Coleman reaching 100 yards and finding the box in his second game would have anyone declaring him a solid RB2 for the rest of the season. But let me at least take a look under the hood regarding his utilization before we pin "league winner" to his name.

Rushing Rate (Week 8): 61.1% (Coleman), 38.9% (Dobbins)

The Broncos ran the ball five times from inside Kansas City's 5-yard line. Not only did Dobbins stay off the field for all of those plays, but Coleman handled four of the carries (Nix took the other). With RJ Harvey on IR, Coleman took all of the third-down plays, too. The situation is lining up for the rookie to take over as the starter as Denver looks to maintain their spot atop the division. And with the Panthers up before their bye, Coleman has a chance to force the decision sooner rather than later.

No Terry? The Commanders Are Still Scary Enough

Early-season returns on Washington's offense highlighted its need for ancillary pass-catchers. Remember, Terry McLaurin and Jayden Daniels were the only Commanders skill players with a top-100 ADP. On the plus side, both rookie Antonio Williams and veteran Stefon Diggs opened '26 with TDs. But McLaurin, at 230 receiving yards, being a handful behind the team lead (Williams – 259), only amplifies how far the team needs to go to find a consistent passing attack. But there was an injury from Week 5 that we took for granted.

Rachaad White's 33-yard run in the fourth quarter was Washington's longest run since Jacory Croskey-Merritt's TD scamper against the Giants in Week 5. Since then, White and Austin Ekeler have taken 21 of the 27 first-down carries. Both are below a 30% rushing success rate. And at least against a good defense, Daniels found himself needing an average of 8.4 yards on third down to convert. Assuming Croskey-Merritt is ready to go by Week 11 , he'll get the Bengals and Cardinals, which should put him back at the RB1 spot. Until then, though, the inefficiencies on the ground have given us more of a glimpse of the passing game.

The Commanders have used 11-personnel groupings on 90.5% of their passing plays over their last two games. Treylon Burks has operated as the X-receiver with 38.0% of Daniels' air yards. As the "McLaurin replacement," Burks will garner the tougher defensive assignments, limiting his weekly output. Typically, we'd turn to the guy getting the lay-up targets, but three different guys have laid claim to those.

Stefon Diggs (Weeks 6-8): 21.0%, 5.5 (aDOT), 71.8% (Slot Rate)

Daniels has looked to the rookie the most on third downs, but Diggs has earned the most looks when the Commanders get into scoring position. At the same time, Okonkwo overlaps both receivers in terms of how often he lines up in the slot and the types of routes he runs.

Daniels has just two games with more than 30 pass attempts. Marcus Mariota only had one. Washington's playstyle already puts a cap on the number of QB dropbacks. And with multiple options at Daniels' disposal, none of them profile as worthwhile starters outside of deep leagues.

articles.title: Lionel Messi magic leads Inter Miami comeback against New England Revolution to secure 2027 Champions Cup berth
articles.summary: Lionel Messi produced another masterclass to guide Inter Miami to a vital 2-1 victory over the New England Revolution. The Argentine's decisive goal ensured...
articles.body:
Lionel Messi produced another masterclass to guide Inter Miami to a vital 2-1 victory over the New England Revolution. The Argentine's decisive goal ensured his team secured a coveted spot in the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup while moving them up to second in the Eastern Conference.

Inter Miami secured their place in the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup with a 2-1 comeback victory over the New England Revolution . Messi proved to be the difference-maker in Foxborough, providing a crucial assist before scoring the decisive winning goal.

The narrow victory helped Miami leapfrog their opponents into second place in the Eastern Conference. They achieved this vital milestone with just one match remaining in the MLS regular season.

The hosts controlled the opening 45 minutes, creating the best opportunities and edging the tactical battle, but the match remained goalless at the break. Daniel Gazdag then opened the scoring for the Revolution early in the second half. Miami responded brilliantly in the 69th minute. Messi delivered a deft backward header to set up German Berterame, who fired the visitors level.

Messi completed the comeback in spectacular fashion. The Argentine forward dribbled past several defenders outside the penalty box before smashing a trademark low, left-footed shot past goalkeeper Matt Turner. The Revolution almost snatched a dramatic late draw when Ian Fray scored an own goal. However, the offside flag quickly rescued Miami and ensured Messi's heroics were not undone.

Miami manager Kily Gonzalez was quick to praise his talismanic captain following the vital victory. "I have no doubt that he's the best of all," he insisted. "Leo at his age and what he does, from my point of view, deserves the MVP and also the Ballon d'Or."

The crucial win means Inter Miami will join Nashville SC, the Vancouver Whitecaps, and the Revolution in the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup. They avoided a high-pressure scenario on Decision Day to secure their qualification. Miami now sit on 59 points from 33 matches. They will finish their regular season campaign with an important home fixture against Charlotte FC.

articles.title: London City Lionesses taught a lesson in ruthlessness as the champions weather the storm
articles.summary: London City Lionesses had the bit between their teeth. They went at the reigning Women’s Super League champions Manchester City like a hurricane, tearing at...
articles.body:
London City Lionesses had the bit between their teeth. They went at the reigning Women's Super League champions Manchester City like a hurricane, tearing at them from all sides.

Within 60 seconds Lucia Corrales was sprinting down Manchester City's left. Jana Fernandez went on a rampaging run only for her shot to veer wide, Grace Geyoro skied the ball over the bar from close range, while visiting defender Rebecca Knaak took the full force of Daniela Arques' sweetly connected strike on her head.

Still they came. Fernandez stormed in at the back post only to miss the target, and then Isobel Goodwin had the best chance of them all, only for centre-back Jade Rose to stand in her way.

London City were suffocating Manchester City, pinning them back and forcing high turnovers. They regained possession in the final third more than any team in the first half of a WSL game this season, according to Opta. But they had nothing to show for it. At half-time, they should have been ahead, but only two of their 12 shots — nine of which came from inside the box — had been on target.

Manchester City weathered the storm and, after the interval, taught London City a lesson: take your chances, otherwise you will be punished.

The difference between the two sides was efficiency. When Lauren Hemp threaded a ball through to Bunny Shaw in the 53rd minute, she pounced. Fernandez's brilliant near-post header 18 minutes from the end was just reward for her side's efforts but, two minutes later, the visitors reminded their hosts of that all-important lesson.

They broke their opponents' press, hit on the transition quickly, and Lauren Hemp's finish was a dagger to London City's hopes.

Even if their team is not on song, nine times out of 10, Shaw and Hemp still deliver: the result of a foundation built over five years of playing alongside each other in the same team.

London City have not struggled to score this season, as shown by their recent 6-1 thrashing of Tottenham Hotspur, but none of those goals came from a No 9.

On Sunday they showed they had the capabilities to beat any WSL side. A fine double save from Mary Earps, starting her first WSL match this season, kept Manchester City at bay in the first half, but their defence was cohesive, their midfield fluid and dominant, while their wingers pose back lines different problems with their movement and pace. They are short of options at centre-back, admittedly, but Maria Perez — usually a midfielder — is covering very well.

The issue is they're missing an out-and-out centre-forward to take the chances they create.

Very few teams have a player like Shaw. Indeed, Chelsea struggled to sign a striker in the summer and eventually decided that Melvine Malard was their best option. London City recruited Nicole Anyomi from Frankfurt, but the 26-year-old has taken time to get up to speed, scoring just once in six matches. Freya Godfrey can play up front too, but Goodwin got the nod on Sunday after impressing with her midweek hat-trick against Crystal Palace.

Exposing Manchester City, however, is a very different prospect.

Goodwin failed to take her chances, and her replacement, Ayomi, made little impact after coming on just after the hour mark. London City's xG of 3.1 was the highest in a WSL home defeat since the 2021-22 season. They dominated the game, as shown below in the threat timeline and territory charts, while the high position of their passing network points to their underlying aggression.

But they ended the afternoon with nothing to show for it.

In contrast to Manchester City, London City have assembled a star-studded side who have only played together in this league for two months.

According to coach Eder Maestre, the difference came down to maturity. That may come as a surprise given he has a three-time Ballon d'Or winner, World Cup winners, a Champions League top goalscorer and several experienced internationals at his disposal. But he was referring to the collective maturity of a newly assembled team in only its second WSL season.

"They (Manchester City) were more used to being in that kind of position," said Maestre. "When you have this consistency and you are very used to playing these kinds of games, you have more experience. That's why maybe we have extra nervousness in the moments that we need to be more clinical."

Ahead of the match, Maestre somewhat surprisingly described this meeting as a "game changer in terms of creating a new chapter at this club" and one which they would approach like a "final".

But as Manchester City's WSL-winning manager Andree Jeglertz knows, a season is not defined by one game. Instead, it is about finding different levels to win week after week. His side suffered the onslaught and took the few chances they had. "They are a great team and will test a lot of teams," said Jeglertz of the hosts. "But to contest you need to compete for the whole season and in other competitions. Then we can talk about it."

When asked how close his team are to the finished article, Maestre added: "In terms of performance, we are there."

London City did not make a statement with the result, but Sunday's display shows they can go toe-to-toe with the best and stretch them. The question is whether they can sustain such performances to secure Champions League qualification.

London City Lionesses LFC, Manchester City WFC, Women's Soccer, Women's Super League

articles.title: Dolphins’ Malik Willis doesn’t hold back on Ollie Gordon’s costly penalty vs. Patriots
articles.summary: The Miami Dolphins faced the New England Patriots on Sunday. Miami put in quite the effort, and it even seemed as if they were going to win. Unfortunately fo...
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins faced the New England Patriots on Sunday. Miami put in quite the effort, and it even seemed as if they were going to win. Unfortunately for Malik Willis and his teammates, this did not pan out the way they hoped.

The Dolphins fell to the New England Patriots on Sunday . In the third quarter, they had a 13-10 lead over New England. They seemed to be in position to keep their drive alive as well. However, an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty by Ollie Gordon pushed them back from third-and-four to third-and-20. Willis was not happy with this, as he expressed after the game .

"I mean, Ollie is a competitor and he cares about the game a lot and I was just letting him know that in that situation, that he's deada** wrong," Willis told reporters, via Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk. "I mean, that's the honest truth. And it would be wrong if I didn't tell him the truth."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Dolphins were unable to convert on the third-and-20 after the penalty. New England took possession of the ball after that. On the ensuing drive, the Patriots marched down the field and took the lead.

It was a lead New England would not relinquish. The Dolphins added a touchdown in the fourth quarter, but it was too little, too late at that point. Miami fell to 1-7 on the season as a result of this defeat.

The Dolphins are looking to recapture some momentum. Their next chance at victory will come on November 8th when the Detroit Lions come to town.

articles.title: Struggling Slavia face Arsenal as grim record looms
articles.summary: Hosting Arsenal in the Champions League on Wednesday, Slavia Prague are facing the mammoth task of ending a drawn-out winless streak in the competition as an...
articles.body:
Hosting Arsenal in the Champions League on Wednesday, Slavia Prague are facing the mammoth task of ending a drawn-out winless streak in the competition as an unwelcome record looms.

The Czech champions have won a single game out of 23 in the Champions League -- on their debut in the competition against Steaua Bucharest in September 2007.

They have since only managed eight draws and 14 losses over four Champions League campaigns including the current one.

"Of course the longer it gets, the more unpleasant it is," said Jindrich Trpisovsky, the Slavia manager since 2017.

"The streak is long and as we keep talking about it, I brood over it more than in the past," he added.

Record holders AEK Athens failed to win 24 straight games from 1992-2006, while Steaua, now known as FCSB, recorded 23 winless games between 2006 and 2013.

Slavia host Arsenal fresh off the back of their 1-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield, which would daunt most teams, before Villarreal at home and Bayern Munich away in their next European games.

"Of course we know how tough European games are and how hard you must work to win," said Trpisovsky.

"In some games we were on the front foot and we got beaten. This is the beauty of football."

Slavia have faced Arsenal three times in the Champions League, recording a draw and two losses including a humiliating 7-0 drubbing in London in 2007.

"Slavia simply face the best teams whose quality is obvious," said Vladimir Smicer, a former Slavia striker who won the Champions League with Liverpool in 2005.

"I think they were unlucky a few times," he told AFP.

Slavia were close to breaking the hoodoo in this year's opener against Lens -- reduced to 10 men, they took a 2-1 lead in the 89th minute but squandered the chance and lost 3-2.

"That's bad luck really. But the streak is unpleasant in any case," said Smicer, who played for Lens from 1996-1999.

"And they are now facing teams like Arsenal and Bayern and these are games you don't expect Slavia to win."

Smicer said Slavia should rather have beaten lower-ranked teams like Sabah to whom they lost 2-0 in Baku in October.

"Slavia has a deep roster so the coach can adapt to the playing style of their opponents, but in the end it's all about quality," he added.

"In Baku they simply underperformed, like in some other games, and that extended the winless streak. There have been games they should have won but unfortunately it didn't happen."

Slavia will host Arsenal on November 4, exactly a year after losing 3-0 to the Gunners in the Champions League at home.

Slavia defender David Zima hailed the competition as "a football university".

"It's the top level and you can't stress out about having to win now. This is simply football and you can't always win. You just need a little luck."

Trpisovsky said everything would have to click into place for Slavia to stand a chance against the giants.

"Everything has to go our way and we need to give 100 percent and then we can succeed in any game."

articles.title: Wales not finished product but all roads lead to 2029
articles.summary: Head coach Sean Lynn says Wales are not the finished product but he has been encouraged by their WXV Global Series.
articles.body:
Head coach Sean Lynn admits Wales are far from the finished product but says he has been hugely encouraged by their WXV showings.

An eight-try mauling of South Africa in Cardiff and two Test wins out in Japan saw Wales finish World Rugby's new Global Series on a high.

Only a narrow two-point defeat by USA - a team ranked in the world's top six - prevented a clean sweep.

It marks quite the transformation for Lynn's side who had been on a nine-Test losing streak prior to the tournament and slumped to an all-time low world ranking of 13th.

"Twelve months ago we didn't win a game in the World Cup. We've worked so hard as a group of players and staff and we've come into this WXV with three out of four wins," said Lynn.

"Are we the finished product? No we're not, but we're seeing the bigger picture of that roadmap to the 2029 World Cup.

"There are areas that we need to be looking at and the players now need to go back to the PWR [Premiership Women's Rugby] and Celtic Challenge because we're still looking to move that dial.

"But I can't fault the effort from players and staff, it's been a really intense 11 weeks."

Wales' transformation began with a brutal pre-season during which Lynn secured the permanent services of assistant coaches Ashley Beck and Steve Salvin.

That, along with Tyrone Holmes' growing impact as defence coach and the introduction of strength and conditioning specialist Gareth Harris, gave Wales some much-needed stability.

"We've all been really specific about what we want to do. We've established a DNA and I'm really proud of all the hard work - physical and mental - that not just the players have put in, but also the staff," said Wales co-captain Kate Williams.

"It's competitive within the team and that's showing on the pitch as well against other teams."

Lynn has capped 12 new players during his 18 months in charge and in doing so has unearthed gems such as Seren Lockwood, Branwen Metcalfe, Freya Bell and Amy Williams.

"It's super important that we are always watching. Amy Williams for instance, what I saw of her at Cardiff Met and Brython Thunder, I really liked," he said.

"She's very brave, likes to get the ball in her hands and always wants to beat that first defender. Individuals like her and Freya Bell have been like ducks to water coming into the international arena and I believe there are more out there.

"The senior players are now having that competitive edge in the squad, and they know that the jersey is not theirs."

Lynn has shown he is not afraid to make big selection calls and has backed the youngsters all summer, with the first glimpse of his new-look side coming in the 34-17 victory over Barbarians .

While Lynn has enjoyed success with fresh blood, it remains unclear as to which is his preferred half-back partnership after experimenting with a few different combinations.

Kayleigh Powell went well at 10 alongside Lockwood against the Barbarians, but a hamstring injury ruled her out of the entire WXV campaign.

Keira Bevan - usually a scrum-half - played 10 against South Africa and Wales looked much better in attack when keeping ball in hand. But a head injury suffered by Lockwood meant we only saw about 30 minutes of that duo.

Lleucu George started at fly-half against USA and in the second Japan Test, with Wales reverting back to a kicking and territorial game.

Hopefully one pair will have a run of games during the 2027 Six Nations, allowing Wales to finally gain some continuity in such pivotal positions.

Not that they needed any extra incentives, but next year's historic women's British and Irish Lions tour would certainly have been in the back of players' minds heading into WXV.

Lions head coach Jo Yapp was at Cardiff Arms Park for Wales' demolition of the Springboks and also attended a training session.

And while the bulk of the team is still likely to be made of England's World Cup-winning stars, there are some Wales players who have put their hand up.

Wales co-captain Alex Callender has been colossal. After missing the Six Nations through injury, the feisty flanker has exploded back onto the international scene, leading from the front with tackles and turnovers.

Prop Sisilia Tuipulotu is also back to her best. She is by far Wales' best ball carrier and has proven very difficult to stop having racked up four tries this autumn.

Bevan has showed Yapp a versatility in being able to play in both half-back positions, although her showing in the first Japan Test was a lot less convincing than against South Africa.

And then if you consider potential bolters, scrum-half Lockwood should be in the conversation. She has an international maturity well beyond her 20 years, is a huge threat at the breakdown and has a good eye for the try-line. She also looks equally as comfortable when moved out to the wing.

Wales have not won a Six Nations game since edging Italy in the final round of the 2024 championship.

An even though they open the 2027 edition against reigning champions England, they will surely take some confidence from their upturn in results.

"I know it's a long way away and a lot can happen, but for us going into the Six Nations and not actually starting against Scotland [which Wales have done for the past three years] is exciting," said Lynn.

"We've got the Red Roses coming to the Principality, it's huge for players and staff."

Until then, Lynn and his staff will be keeping a watchful eye on the domestic leagues, which Callender says players head back to with "confidence".

Reflecting on the year a whole, she said: "It's always a privilege to be able to wear the jersey and I'm just so proud of the girls.

"It's been a roller coaster, but it's all part of the sport isn't it?"

Let's hope the ride in 2027 will be just as enjoyable, with more ups than downs.

images.caption: Keira Bevan and Lleucu George are Wales' most experienced half-back partnership [Huw Evans Picture Agency]

articles.title: Washington Commanders Week 8 Player of the Game: RB Rachaad White
articles.summary: Commanders running back Rachaad White is Washington's Player of the Game in their 27-10 win against the Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body:
For most of their Sunday Night Football game against the Philadelphia Eagles , the Washington Commanders were in control. After the Eagles scored 10 in the first quarter, Washington shut them out in the next three quarters and won 27-10.

The Commanders' defense played a key role in this game, holding Philadelphia to just 268 total yards and generating two turnovers, one of which was on a fourth-down stop late in the fourth quarter. However, it was running back Rachaad White's drive that sealed the win for Washington, making him the player of the game.

Throughout the game, the Commanders split reps between Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler, both expected to step up with starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt on injured reserve. Both performed well, but White carried the load on the final drive to seal the win.

First, his 33-yard run put the Commanders at the Eagles' four-yard line. He had the next two rushing attempts, getting it in from one yard out to score Washington's second touchdown of the game. That was also their first rushing touchdown since their tie against the New York Giants . Without this crucial drive from White, the Commanders would have had to settle for a field goal, which would have kept it a two-possession game, giving Philadelphia a chance to possibly come back and win.

White also maintained his position as a pass-catching running back, although he finished with just two receptions for five yards. Ironically, he also did that when Washington faced the Eagles in the season opener. Still, he was a crucial part of this offense and played a large role in securing the victory for the Commanders.

Washington will play their next game against the Los Angeles Rams with a chance to build on the momentum from this 17-point win. This was also their first win by at least three possessions since they defeated the Los Angeles Chargers 27-10 last year.

Washington's defense, which was outstanding, had several player-of-the-game contenders, sacking Tanner McKee five times and forcing two turnovers. But White gets the edge over quarterback Jayden Daniels for our Week 8 Player of the Game.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino has a USMNT roster dilemma, and the 2028 Olympics are making it more complicated
articles.summary: With his strikers, healthy again, and a dozen newcomers having impressed this fall, Mauricio Pochettino must decide who faces Haiti in the Nations League qua...
articles.body:
Mauricio Pochettino's U.S. roster announcement for the first official matches since the World Cup is days away, but beyond decisions common before every international window, he must also sort out whether his young prospects belong with the first team or the junior platoon with Olympic medal aspirations.

Starting Nov. 9, the squads will gather separately — Pochettino's for the CONCACAF Nations League's quarterfinals against Haiti and Steve Cherundolo's under-23s for a head start on the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

Had Pochettino not invited a dozen newcomers to senior camp six weeks ago, the intrigue this week wouldn't rise above a typical selection. During victories over Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada, however, several showed they were up to the challenge.

In all likelihood, many will join Cherundolo for what is expected to be an overseas camp and friendlies. Cherundolo worked with Pochettino's staff at the last camp, and the two coaches are collaborating on this week's selections.

With greater public attention on an Olympics at home, the U.S. Soccer Federation has placed extra emphasis on building a strong team. (Olympic men's soccer is restricted to players 23 and under, with three overage exceptions.) Cherundolo will conduct additional camps in many of the international windows over the next 18 months.

At the moment, Pochettino might need to peel off a few players for this camp at the national training center in the Atlanta area, followed by games against Haiti on Nov. 14 in Miami and Nov. 17 in Cincinnati. (The U.S. has never failed to advance to the final four.)

The frontline sits at the forefront of Pochettino's decisions.

After missing the September-October call-up to recover from injuries, top strikers Folarin Balogun and Ricardo Pepi scored over the weekend as second-half subs for Monaco and PSV Eindhoven, respectively. (Pepi also assisted during the 7-0 romp over Willem II.)

It was the first goal since the World Cup's round of 32 for Balogun, who has played just 116 minutes in Ligue 1 for Monaco. Pepi returned Saturday after missing six weeks with a muscular injury.

Both are involved in European competition this week: Eindhoven hosts Club Brugge on Wednesday in the Champions League and Monaco faces Nordsjaelland on Thursday in the third-tier Conference League.

Christian Pulisic, whose injury recovery and limited playing time at AC Milan kept him out of the previous U.S. camp, scored the opening goal four minutes into a 3-1 win over rival Inter Milan on Saturday. Pulisic and Milan are back at it Thursday against Ferencvaros in the second-tier Europa League.

Barring any setbacks, Pochettino seems inclined to summon the trio for the first consequential action since the World Cup's round of 16 against Belgium.

In the recent four friendlies, teenagers Justin Ellis (Orlando) and Julian Hall (Red Bull New York) started two games apiece at striker. Ellis scored in the first and last matches, and Hall struck in each of the first three.

Seven of the 12 U.S. goals were scored by teenagers.

Pepi's replacement, St. Louis' Damion Downs, 22, was the third striker.

If Pochettino is seeking a short-term fix at striker, he could consider Vancouver's Brian White, 30, who scored twice Sunday to raise his season total to 20, six off Lionel Messi's MLS-best pace. White (66 goals in 114 MLS matches the past four years) scored once in seven U.S. appearances in 2025.

Pulisic's absence this fall opened an opportunity for Philadelphia's Cavan Sullivan, who, at 17, became the youngest scorer in program history. European-based wingers Mathis Albert, 17, and Zavier Gozo, 19, also debuted.

Sullivan, though, missed two matches with an ankle injury before returning this weekend as a sub, while Albert and Gozo aren't playing regularly for Borussia Dortmund and Crystal Palace, respectively.

Other World Cup players to miss the recent friendlies included midfielder Weston McKennie, winger Tim Weah, attacker Brenden Aaronson and right back/wing Joe Scally.

McKennie was poised to return to the U.S. squad before leaving Juventus' match at halftime Sunday with a reported adductor injury. The severity is unclear.

Scally has a strong recall case: He leads Mönchengladbach with three Bundesliga goals and has posted two goals and two assists in the past five matches across all competitions. (On Saturday, he had a goal overturned by video replay.)

Midfielders Tanner Tessmann (Lyon) and Johnny Cardoso (Atlético Madrid) are angling for recalls after missing the World Cup, but Pochettino doesn't seem to rate Tessmann very high and Cardoso is nursing another injury.

And then there is Jack McGlynn, a 23-year-old right wing for Stoke City in the second-tier English Championship. He played 12 times for the U.S. in 2025 but wasn't in the World Cup mix. On Saturday, he had a goal and an assist in a 2-0 victory over Preston North End, lifting his totals in the past seven appearances to three goals and two assists.

Four Americans are employed by the English Championship front-runner, Middlesbrough. Midfielder Sebastian Berhalter continues to impress in his first season overseas with a goal and an assist in the first half of a 3-0 victory over Charlton Athletic.

Aidan Morris, who missed the World Cup cut, is a defensive-midfield mainstay, while summer signing Max Arfsten, a World Cup wing back, is coming off the bench. Midfielder Rokas Pukstas has played once since signing in September.

Only Berhalter is all but certain to receive a U.S. callback.

The other U.S. goal scorer over the weekend was 20-year-old winger Cole Campbell, on a spectacular strike for Elversberg in the Bundesliga. Because of an injury, his debut at the last camp had to wait until the second half of the last match.

At center back, Auston Trusty has missed four matches for family reasons and Miles Robinson has missed six with a leg injury. Trusty might be in uniform Thursday against Besiktas in the Europa League. Mark McKenzie, a World Cup member and Toulouse starter, is available after being left out last time.

Alex Freeman continues to soar for La Liga's Villarreal, which on Tuesday will host Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League.

The U.S. goalkeeping situation remains unsettled after all four call-ups started once during the last window. New England's Matt Turner, the 2022 World Cup starter and 2026 back-up, is enjoying a strong MLS season and could rejoin the team after Pochettino passed him over the last camp.

The only Olympic-eligible keeper at that last camp, 20-year-old Diego Kochen, was the best of the bunch.

Seeking another U.S. call-up is Nashville's Brian Schwake, who on Sunday, stopped a penalty kick for an MLS-best third time.

Pochettino and Cherundolo are probably going to announce their rosters at least a day apart late this week.
